overview: Fukuiraptor (meaning 'Fukui plunderer') was a medium-sized carnivorous theropod from the Early Cretaceous of Japan, living approximately 127–113 million years ago. Estimated at around 4.2 metres in length, it is known from the Kitadani Formation of Fukui Prefecture and possibly the Sebayashi Formation. Fukuiraptor kitadaniensis holds the distinction of being the first carnivorous dinosaur described from Japan, and its discovery significantly advanced understanding of Cretaceous Asian theropod diversity.

Described by Azuma and Currie in 2000, Fukuiraptor was initially interpreted as a dromaeosaurid, but subsequent analyses place it within Megaraptora (Neovenatoridae) or as closely related to Australovenator of Australia. This placement suggests Fukuiraptor belonged to a group of medium-to-large theropods that achieved a wide distribution across Asia and Gondwana during the Cretaceous, making it important for understanding megaraptoran biogeography.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: Fukuiraptor kitadaniensis was described by Yoichi Azuma and Philip Currie in 2000 based on material from the Kitadani quarry in Fukui Prefecture, a region that has yielded Japan's richest dinosaur fauna. The genus name honours Fukui Prefecture, and the species name references the Kitadani Formation. Initial material included theropod teeth, claws, and partial skeletal elements.

articles.title: Revised Phylogenetic Placement
articles.body: Early descriptions placed Fukuiraptor as a large dromaeosaurid because its large hand claws superficially resembled those of raptor dinosaurs. However, more thorough analysis of postcranial anatomy — particularly limb proportions and vertebral features — indicates Fukuiraptor belongs within Megaraptora, a clade of medium-to-large theropods. The Wikipedia entry notes it may be one of the basalmost megaraptorans or a sister to Australovenator.

articles.title: Japan's First Carnivore
articles.body: Before Fukuiraptor, Japan's dinosaur record consisted primarily of herbivores and fragmentary material. Its formal description established Japan as a source of carnivorous theropod fossils comparable to those from China and Mongolia, and stimulated further excavation in Fukui Prefecture that would later yield additional theropods and the iguanodontid Fukuisaurus.

articles.title: Megaraptoran Distribution
articles.body: Megaraptorans are now known from Asia (Fukuiraptor), Australia (Australovenator), and South America (Megaraptor, Aerosteon), reflecting a Gondwanan and pan-Cretaceous distribution. The group is characterised by enlarged hand claws used for prey capture, rather than the foot claws typical of dromaeosaurids. Their wide distribution suggests long-distance dispersal or an origin predating Gondwana's breakup.

record.description: Fukuiraptor kitadaniensis was a medium-sized bipedal predatory megaraptoran from the Kitadani Formation of Japan. It is represented by a partial type skeleton and additional fragmentary individuals, including juveniles; early allosauroid interpretations are outdated.
facts: The holotype is a partial skeleton, not a complete mounted animal.
The large hand claw was initially mistaken for a foot claw.
Megaraptoran relationships remain debated between allosauroid and coelurosaur/tyrannosauroid hypotheses.

review.ageReviewNote: Restricted to the Aptian Kitadani Formation; referrals outside it are not used to extend the range.
